To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the exocyst complex subunits sec8 and sec10 bind to PSD-90, and this binding is regulated by cypins (cytosolic postsynaptic density 95 (PSD95) interactor).
the exocyst complex subunits sec6 and sec8 interact with PSD-95 and that the interaction of sec8 with PSD-95 is modulated by the cytosolic PDZ-interacting protein.

the sec8 subunit of the exocyst complex binds to the C-terminal PDZ domains of PSD-95 in a sequence-specific manner, and the binding of sec8 to PSD-95 is modulated by the cytosolic PDZ-interacting protein cypin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of sec8 with the postsynaptic density scaffold protein, PSD-95, via the PDZ domains in PSD-95.
the identification of a novel interaction between the exocyst complex sub-unit sec8 and postsynaptic density 95 (PSD 95).
the identification of novel binding partners for PSD-95, which may be involved in the assembly of signalling complexes in the postsynaptic density.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sec8 binds to PSD-95 and this interaction is regulated by cyp
the cytoskeletal protein PSD-95 interacts with the exocyst complex subunits Sec8 and Sec10.
sec8 and cytosolic PSD95 interactor may compete for the binding to PDZ domains of PSD-95.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exocyst complex subunits may play a role in regulating synaptic plasticity by interacting with the postsynaptic density.
the cytoskeletal and membrane trafficking machinery are intimately associated with each other, and that this association may be regulated by the cytosolic PDZ domain protein cypin.
the cytoskeleton-associated exocyst complex subunits, including sec8, may be important components of the postsynaptic density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sec8 can bind to the PDZ domains in PSD-95, which is consistent with our finding that sec8 is present in brain regions enriched in PSD-95 and in the same subcellualr fraction as PSD-95.
the exocyst complex may be a new member of the PSD-95 signalling complex.
sec8 and cytosolic PSD95 interactor compete for binding to PSD-95.
